def: A model that assigns a probability to the next piece of text given the text so far.
Generative Pre-trained Transformer: an autoregressive language model built from decoder-only Transformer blocks.
Producing text one token at a time, appending each chosen token to the context before predicting the next.
A run of T consecutive tokens used as input, paired with the same run shifted by one token as the targets, so it supplies T prediction problems at once.
Several independent windows stacked into one (B, T) array so they are processed by the same matrix multiplications.
The loss on held-out text the model never trains on, used to judge whether it has learned something general.
Adam with weight decay applied directly to the weights instead of through the gradient.
Raising the learning rate gradually from near zero over the first steps, while the optimiser's running statistics are still unreliable.
A learning-rate schedule that falls from its peak to a small fraction of it along half a cosine wave.
Scaling all gradients down when their global norm exceeds a limit, so one unusual batch cannot cause an enormous update.
A test that compares backward-pass gradients with finite-difference slopes of the loss on a tiny model.
A debugging test: train on a single small batch and confirm the loss falls to nearly zero, which shows the whole pipeline can learn.
A test that changes one input token and checks that only the outputs at that position and later ones change.
